title: Learning a line
line: Know why each move is played. Moves learned by heart fall apart when the other side plays something else.

steps.text: A line you may know: in the Italian Game, the pawn moves to c3 to get ready for a pawn on d4.
Here Black brought out the knight instead of the bishop. The knight attacks your pawn on e4.
Before playing the move you learned, ask what Black's last move does, and answer it.

wrong.c2c3: That is the move from the line you learned. Here it leaves the pawn on e4, and the knight takes it.

steps.hint: Guard the pawn the knight attacks, or make a stronger threat of your own.
steps.after: The pawn is safe, or you have a threat of your own.

steps.text: Another one, from the Vienna Game: when Black's knight is on f6 and takes the pawn on f4, the pawn push chases that knight.
Here Black brought out the other knight first, and then took the pawn on f4.
Ask what is different before you push the pawn from memory, and play a move that fits this position.

wrong.e4e5: That is the move you learned, but no knight stands on f6 to chase, and the knight on c6 takes your pawn.

steps.hint: Your other knight stops a check from the black queen.
steps.after: The move you learned fits one position, not every one. Know why each move is played.

summary: Learn the reason behind each move. When the other side plays something else, the reason tells you what to do.
